title: Miles's saxophonists after Coltrane; Sam Rivers

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Wayne Shorter. First George Colemen, Wayne Shorter, Ron Carter, Tony Williams.
The thing that really surprised me was when Sam Rivers was with him for a while.

I was just talking with somebody. I was talking to Joe Bowie about that. Sam was with Miles for a second. Actually, I thought that that would be nice, a nice change from – because, you know, Miles had trouble finding another saxophone player after Coltrane. He didn’t like Wayne Shorter in the beginning. Coltrane kept trying to get him the gig, Wayne, but he didn’t like Wayne in the beginning, and he didn’t like hardly anybody.
He tried Sonny Stitt. He tried Hank Mobley. He went through a lot of cats. Sam Rivers was one of the guys that he went through. George Coleman.
The problem is with George Coleman, I think, because of the little hip drummer.
Tony Williams. He didn’t get along with George?
Yeah, for some reason. He was in another bag or something. I don’t know.
He liked – he’s the one who got Sam Rivers in, Tony Williams.
Because he used to play with Sam in Boston. So he brought Sam in. But I think Sam was too progressive for Miles. Sam had some other stuff.
